title: Detecting DNS over HTTPS based data exfiltration

value.name: lab-generated DoH traffic
value.quote: We set up three virtual machines running Ubuntu 20.04 as the operating system. Two virtual machines

datasets_evaluated.evidence: We set up three virtual machines running Ubuntu 20.04 as the operating system. Two virtual machines are located in Seattle and the other in Singapore. All virtual machines are configured with public IP addresses

label_source.evidence: To configure the DoH tunneling, we register a domain with Godaddy, use the virtual machine in Seattle as the Name Server (NS) for that domain, and run the server-side program of DNSExfiltrator [32] on this virtual machine

label_feature_overlap.evidence: We analyze the features of DoH tunneling, extract flow-based features from encrypted traffic that contain DNS queries/responses, and build classifiers to detect DoH tunneling.

features_used.evidence: TLS fingerprints of DoH clients are first used for providing the preliminary warning, and then flow-based features of the DoH flow are extracted and used by classifiers to accurately detect DoH tunneling.

feature_groups.evidence: We reassemble the DoH traffic trace to flows and extract flow-level statistical features based on the packet size, timestamp, and direction in each flow.

cert_fields_read.evidence: Therefore, we only focus on unencrypted features from the DoH traffic to perform data exfiltration detection in this work.

fingerprints_used.evidence: We perform extensive TLS fingerprinting measurement on clients that currently supports DoH to fill this gap.

model_family.value: Boosted Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression
model_family.evidence: We select three interpretable supervised models: Boosted Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Logistic Regression (LR).
